title: 1978 AHSME Problem 16
statement: In a room containing \(N\) people, \(N\gt3,\) at least one person has not shaken hands with everyone else in the room. What is the maximum number of people in the room that could have shaken hands with everyone else?

solutions.text:
If one person has missed a handshake, the other person in that missed pair also has not shaken hands with everyone. Thus at most \(N-2\) people can have shaken hands with everyone. This is attainable when exactly two people fail to shake hands with each other and every other handshake occurs. Since \(N-2\) is not listed, the answer is “none of these.”

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: A missed handshake always involves two people
Find an upper bound, then realize it by omitting just one handshake
